title: Short-Term Effects of Manual Therapy Prior to Neuromotor Therapy in Children With Cerebral Palsy
official: Short-Term Effects of Lower Limb Manual Therapy as a Preparatory Phase for Neuromotor Functional Therapy in Children With Spastic Cerebral Palsy: A Prospective Self-Controlled Pilot Study
summary: This pilot study aims to evaluate the immediate, short-term biomechanical and neuromuscular effects of lower limb manual therapy applied as a preparatory phase prior to functional neuromotor rehabilitation in children with spastic cerebral palsy (hemiplegic and diplegic forms). Using a prospective self-controlled design, 20 children will be assessed under four experimental conditions (baseline, post-manual therapy, post-functional therapy, and post-combined manual + functional therapy) to determine if manual techniques enhance gait parameters and motor execution.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of spastic Cerebral Palsy with lower limb involvement (hemiplegia or diplegia).
* Age between 12 months and 10 years.
* Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) level I, II, III, or IV.
* Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) score ≤ 3 in the lower limbs.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Botulinum toxin injection in the lower limbs within the past 6 months.
* Prior functional orthopedic or neurosurgical procedures on the lower limbs.
* Concurrent participation in other experimental clinical studies involving the lower limbs.
* Cognitive impairment preventing comprehension of required motor tasks.
